title: Ambient-pressure, room-temperature superconductivity in a useful ceramic conductor

concept.text: The innovation would be a ceramic conductor that superconducts at ambient pressure at an ordinary room operating temperature and carries useful electrical current through a polycrystalline body. Its defining advance would combine a sufficiently high superconducting temperature with practical fabrication and current transport across many grain boundaries. A high transition temperature measured in a small single crystal would establish only part of that capability.

The proposed scope includes ceramics made through powder or film processing, rather than material recovered from a diamond-anvil cell. It permits ceramic superconductors beyond the oxide-cuprate family. An oxide-cuprate realization would extend the family represented by HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8+δ, usually abbreviated Hg1223; another ceramic chemistry could satisfy the same functional goal.

There are two temperature milestones within this proposal. Superconductivity above 273.15 K would establish operation above the ice point, the minimum demonstration originally proposed. The retained room-temperature title describes a stronger practical ambition: operation at the actual room temperature of the intended application, with sufficient temperature margin. Crossing the ice point alone would not establish that ambition or eliminate refrigeration.

significance.text: Superconductivity above the liquid-nitrogen temperature of approximately 77 K is already a historical achievement. The supplied Hg1223 paper recounts 93 K superconductivity in YBa2Cu3O7 in 1987 and a previous ambient-pressure record of 133 K in Hg1223 in 1993. The revolutionary step proposed here is therefore useful ceramic superconducting transport above the ice point and ultimately at ordinary room operating temperatures, rather than merely another crossing of 77 K.

Conditional engineering significance: a successful above-ice-point conductor would demonstrate superconducting current transport without cooling below the freezing point of water. A realization that operates at the surrounding room temperature could remove the need for refrigeration to maintain superconductivity in its demonstrated conditions. Combining that temperature capability with useful transport across grain boundaries would connect a materials discovery to a manufacturable conductor, placing the advance within ceramics engineering, superconductivity physics and electrical engineering.

Potential applications include cables with greatly reduced resistive conductor losses, magnets and superconducting electronics. These outcomes would still depend on current capacity, magnetic-field tolerance, operating-temperature margin, stability, fabrication and device design. Zero resistance in a specimen does not establish zero total losses in a complete cable under every operating mode, and an elevated transition temperature alone does not establish that a magnet can be compact or useful. The Hg1223 report itself identifies stability and specimen requirements as obstacles between a metastable superconducting state and utilization.

Conditional downstream possibilities include changes to fusion magnets, broader substitution for copper conductors and new quantum devices. None follows automatically from the proposed materials demonstration. Each would require its own system engineering, and some could require additional material capabilities beyond high operating temperature. Room-temperature superconductivity would also not, by itself, establish room-temperature operation of an entire quantum device.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in this proposal is the combination of high operating temperature, ambient pressure and useful current transport in a processed polycrystalline ceramic. The supplied evidence documents progress on some of these dimensions separately, but does not demonstrate their combination. It also does not provide an exhaustive basis for declaring that every possible material remained below the target as of 1 November 2026.

One scientific barrier is obtaining and stabilizing a superconducting state at a sufficiently high temperature without maintaining extreme pressure. The supplied Hg1223 paper cites LaH10 superconductivity up to 260 K under 190 GPa in 2019, illustrating the pressure burden of that hydride result. Its own pressure-quench strategy seeks to preserve pressure-enhanced superconductivity after pressure release, but the reported ambient-pressure onset of 151 K remains far below the ice point. These are distinct obstacles: releasing pressure does not necessarily deliver a sufficiently high operating temperature, and a pressure-created state must also remain stable.

A separate engineering barrier is carrying useful current through the interfaces between ceramic grains. The research identifies cuprate grain boundaries as potential weak links, motivating the explicit intergranular-transport requirement. However, the supplied review retained no text from the cited 2002 grain-boundary review, so the strength, scope and present-day limits of that generalization could not be reassessed. The proposal preserves grain-boundary transport as a capability to demonstrate without treating the unavailable citation as proof that all ceramic grain boundaries have the same limitation.

Proposed engineering requirements extend beyond identifying a transition: the material must be fabricated into a useful geometry, retain its superconducting properties in air, carry current under the intended magnetic field and remain stable over a stated service interval. For pressure-stabilized phases, maintaining the relevant state during handling and characterization is an additional challenge. The Hg1223 study explicitly identifies improvements in stability, sample size and surface condition as necessary for further characterization and utilization; those observations concern its metastable material rather than every possible ceramic realization.

current_state.text: Liangzi Deng and coauthors, including Ching-Wu Chu, reported pressure-quenched Hg1223 with an ambient-pressure superconducting onset temperature up to 151 K. The research dates the preprint to 12 March 2026 and identifies a subsequent Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences citation, volume 123, article e2536178123. The supplied review assessed retained manuscript text and supporting information associated with the arXiv record. The paper places its result against the 133 K ambient-pressure record dating to 1993, already well above 77 K. At 151 K, the reported onset is −122.15 °C.

The 151 K figure must be interpreted as an onset transition temperature, which the manuscript explicitly specifies for its cited transition temperatures. It does not establish zero resistance and a Meissner response together at 151 K, nor a useful ceramic conductor at that temperature. The reported experiments used five samples, S1–S5, approximately 100–130 μm in size, cut from three self-flux-grown Hg1223 single crystals. They therefore do not demonstrate transport through many grain boundaries in a processed polycrystalline conductor. The supplied review did not inspect plotted curves or independently reanalyze raw data.

The nickelate research line provides a further example of superconductivity under high pressure. The arXiv landing page for “Bulk superconductivity up to 96 K in pressurized nickelate single crystals” records an initial submission on 24 January 2025 and a revision on 21 April 2026. Its revised abstract reports up to 96 K. The retained 17-page manuscript, identified in the review as the same research line through its authors and bilayer nickelate compositions, instead reports an earlier 91 K result and describes both zero resistance and a Meissner effect under high pressure. The two temperatures belong to different supplied versions; the 96 K figure cannot be attributed to the retained manuscript. Neither version demonstrates the ambient-pressure, above-ice-point polycrystalline capability proposed here.

For LK-99, the research supplies a 2025 Chemistry of Materials abstract summary stating that the studied apatite remains a wide-bandgap insulator and excluding superconducting mechanisms that require it to be metallic. No article artifact was retained for the supplied review, so that specific interpretation could not be checked against the paper. Even as summarized, its mechanism-dependent conclusion should not be expanded into an unrestricted statement about every possible superconducting mechanism or ceramic composition.

The supplied evidence establishes dated reports and their stated experimental scope, rather than a complete survey through 1 November 2026. No bounded freshness search was supplied, so the original universal assertion that no confirmed material superconducts at ambient pressure above 0 °C cannot be established from this record. That limitation does not show that the assertion is false, and it does not invalidate the dated Hg1223 report. Independent replication of the 151 K onset result is also not established by the supplied material.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed minimum demonstration: a polycrystalline ceramic made through powder or film processing, rather than recovered from a diamond-anvil cell, should exhibit both zero resistance and a Meissner effect above 273.15 K at ambient pressure in air. Both diagnostics should be established in the claimed operating range, rather than assigning the entire result the temperature of an onset feature. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not an established consensus standard. The paired diagnostics have precedent in the supplied high-pressure nickelate report.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed minimum demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed conductor demonstration: the material should transport current across many grain boundaries at a level useful for a specified cable or magnet demonstration. The report should identify specimen geometry, processing route, grain structure, temperature, magnetic field, current and stability conditions so that usefulness is assessable. No universal critical-current number is proposed: the relevant requirement depends on the stated application. A small single crystal or a result above 77 K but far below 273.15 K would not satisfy this minimum scope.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed conductor demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed room-temperature demonstration: satisfying the retained title would additionally require superconducting transport at a specified ordinary room operating temperature, with a stated margin and under the intended application conditions. An above-ice-point result below that operating temperature would be an important intermediate achievement, but would not establish operation without refrigeration in that environment. Claims about complete cables, magnets or electronics would require corresponding device demonstrations.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed room-temperature demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent groups should reproduce the synthesis, superconducting diagnostics and intergranular transport using multiple specimens or batches. Reports should disclose failed preparations, measurement limits and changes during handling or storage, and provide sufficient methods and data for independent assessment. Testing across stated temperatures, fields, currents and durations would establish demonstrated breadth within those conditions; finite tests would not establish universal performance or indefinite stability.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CRM-01, room-temperature tensile ductility in bulk polycrystalline structural ceramics, and CRM-12, large transparent ceramics approaching theoretical failure strength, share an interest in ceramic microstructure and interfaces. Their defining outcomes are mechanical deformation or strength and transparency; CRM-06 requires superconducting electrical transport. Better mechanical properties could help conductor handling, but would not establish superconductivity.

Roster-based synthesis: CRM-04, densification without a high-temperature furnace cycle, and CRM-11, net-shape additive manufacturing of fully dense technical ceramics, overlap with CRM-06 through processing and component fabrication. Either could become an enabling route if compatible with a superconducting material. Density, shape control or reduced processing temperature alone would not establish the required superconducting phase or current transport across grain boundaries.

Roster-based synthesis: CRM-03, ceramic electrolytes for lithium-metal solid-state cells, and CRM-10, oxide ceramics that turn sunlight and water into fuel, also concern functional ceramics for energy systems. CRM-03 centers on ionic transport and battery interfaces, CRM-10 on light-driven fuel production, and CRM-06 on superconducting electrical conduction. Their transport and stability challenges can overlap without making their completion criteria interchangeable.

Roster-based synthesis: CRM-02, load-bearing ceramics for long service in air above the silica limit; CRM-05, repeated restoration of strength after critical cracks; and CRM-08, stoichiometric silicon-carbide fibers and composites at general industrial cost, could inform durability, supporting structures or manufacturability. None supplies the high-temperature superconducting state or intergranular current capability that defines CRM-06.

Roster-based synthesis: CRM-07, a low-activation structural ceramic retaining heat transport after fusion-relevant irradiation, shares a possible fusion application with CRM-06. Its target is structural and thermal performance under irradiation, whereas CRM-06 could contribute to magnet conductors if additional field, current and stability requirements were met. CRM-09, ceramic membranes replacing cryogenic olefin–paraffin distillation, shares the prospect of reducing refrigeration burdens, but does so through selective separation rather than superconductivity. Each remains a distinct innovation.

change_log.change: Preserved CRM-06 and its title while distinguishing the proposed above-ice-point minimum from the stronger room-temperature ambition.
change_log.reason: 273.15 K marks the ice point; exceeding it does not establish operation at ordinary room temperature or eliminate refrigeration.

change_log.change: Replaced the universal present-day absence claim with a bounded account of the supplied evidence.
change_log.reason: The empty freshness record cannot establish that no confirmed material met the threshold through 1 November 2026.

change_log.change: Expanded the Hg1223 account to include onset terminology, sample sizes, single-crystal scope, historical context and stability limitations.
change_log.reason: These details distinguish the reported 151 K result from paired superconducting diagnostics and a practical polycrystalline conductor demonstration.

change_log.change: Separated the revised nickelate landing page's 96 K report from the retained manuscript's earlier 91 K result.
change_log.reason: The supplied artifacts represent different versions; attributing 96 K to the retained manuscript would misstate the evidence.

change_log.change: Retained the grain-boundary motivation and LK-99 discussion with explicit access limitations.
change_log.reason: Neither cited article had a retained artifact for review. Missing evidence warrants qualification rather than deletion or a finding that the assertions are false.

change_log.change: Recast cables, magnets, electronics, fusion and quantum applications as conditional outcomes with practical requirements.
change_log.reason: A temperature transition and zero specimen resistance do not establish complete-system losses, useful field performance or device readiness.

change_log.change: Replaced the narrow 1986 oxide-cuprate framing with the documented 1987 and 1993 milestones and a broader ceramic scope.
change_log.reason: The supplied review supports those milestones, while the proposed innovation permits ceramic chemistries beyond oxide cuprates.

change_log.change: Added explicit proposed reproducibility, operating-condition and device-level criteria, and explained relationships to every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: The record needs assessable completion boundaries and clear conceptual distinctions without treating proposed thresholds as established standards.

unresolved_issues: Whether any confirmed material met the ambient-pressure, above-ice-point or room-temperature target by 1 November 2026 remains unresolved without a supplied freshness survey.

Independent replication and the relationship between the reported 151 K onset and zero resistance or magnetic response at that temperature are not established by the supplied review; curves and raw data were not independently evaluated.
The revised nickelate result of 96 K remains unmatched to the retained manuscript, which reports 91 K.
The detailed scope of the cuprate grain-boundary limitation and the LK-99 paper's mechanism-dependent conclusions remain unverified because their article artifacts were not retained.

The proposal specifies neither an ordinary room operating temperature nor application-specific current, field, stability, lifetime and manufacturing requirements. These must be defined before claiming full room-temperature conductor completion.
